strengths: Novel theoretical framework elegantly combining homeostasis and energy constraints that generalizes existing optimal population coding models as special cases
Sophisticated integration of biophysical simulation (NEURON), mathematical optimization, and empirical neural data to ground abstract models in ATP metabolism
Clean analytical solutions (Table 1) for multiple coding objectives demonstrating mathematical tractability without sacrificing biological realism
Successfully predicts tuning curve flattening under metabolic stress, whereas prior models only predict shortening or widening, providing unified explanation for empirical phenomena
Generates specific testable predictions about ion channel properties under metabolic constraint that can be validated via electrophysiology experiments
Comprehensive appendices with detailed derivations, simulation parameters, and code facilitate reproducibility and transparency
weaknesses: Empirical validation limited to single dataset (Padamsey et al. 2022 mouse visual cortex) with one primary data point (32% widening); no cross-dataset or cross-system validation demonstrated

Cumulative approximation effects not systematically analyzed: tiling assumption, approximate homeostasis (Eq. 5), Gaussian tuning curves, and independence assumptions each introduce errors whose interaction is unclear

Biophysical simulation uses oversimplified single-compartment model varying only three parameters; 8-degree polynomial fits to noise (Sec. H.4) raise overfitting concerns; fitted parameters show noticeable deviations for κ > 130
Model parameters determined post-hoc from simulation data: value α=1 derived by observing E^(1/α) proportionality in simulation, potentially limiting theoretical foundation
Comparisons to existing models (Fig. 4) modify those frameworks for comparison fairness; lacking ablation studies demonstrating necessity of proposed components
Missing robustness analysis: no sensitivity studies on key parameters, no systematic evaluation of approximation validity boundaries, no behavior analysis outside fitted parameter ranges
Scope limited to visual cortex neurons under two metabolic states (29% energy reduction); generalization to other brain regions, organisms, or metabolic conditions undemonstrated
Noise dispersion model requires refitting κ-dependent parameters for each activity level, limiting practical applicability and generalization to new contexts

strengths: Biophysically grounded approach connecting ATP consumption to cell parameters via realistic NEURON simulations, more sophisticated than spike-rate-only constraints in prior work
Elegant theoretical framework showing how existing models (Ganguli & Simoncelli [5], Wang et al. [30]) emerge as special cases, providing unifying perspective
Well-motivated problem addressing understudied phenomenon of firing rate homeostasis under metabolic stress with clear mathematical formulation and rigorous derivations
Explains empirical observation from Padamsey et al. [22] better than existing models, predicting tuning curve flattening rather than shortening or widening
weaknesses: Severely limited empirical validation: only single dataset (mouse L2/3 visual cortex under food restriction) with no independent replication or cross-system validation; no new experiments despite claiming testable predictions

Central approximations are unvalidated: tiling approximation validity unclear across parameter space; approximate homeostasis shows 0.2-2% violations depending on prior; smoothness assumptions quantitatively undefined

Biophysical simulation is oversimplified and may not generalize: single-compartment neuron, response to isolated spike at t=0 rather than realistic spike trains, g_syn calibration procedure may introduce artifacts, degree-8 polynomial fits for η_κ lack cross-validation

Model parameters tied to specific NEURON simulation: α=1 derived from affine relationship dependent on exact simulation details; complex κ-dependent η_κ functions (five fitted parameters) unlikely to transfer to other neuron types; unclear applicability beyond simulated mouse cortex

Weak experimental predictions: claimed relationships between v_rest and g_leak are complex κ-dependent curves (Fig. 3g) without quantitative predictions; future patch-clamp experiments mentioned but not designed; verification strategy unclear
Questionable claim of uniqueness: assertion that method 'uniquely captures' tuning curve flattening is overstated; any model combining energy constraints with homeostasis would predict this

Limited theoretical novelty: extends existing Fisher Information frameworks incrementally; 'optimal decay path' assumption (Eq. 15) lacks biological justification; independence assumption ignored despite known ubiquity of neural correlations

Presentation and reproducibility issues: abrupt transitions between analytical and biophysical sections; many arbitrary hyperparameter choices (polynomial degrees, fit ranges); statistical analysis lacks rigor (no confidence intervals, cross-validation, or significance tests)

strengths: Biophysically grounded framework: ATP consumption is connected to mathematical constraints via NEURON simulation, bridging theory and biology in a principled way
Elegant theoretical unification: Shows how prior models (Ganguli & Simoncelli, Wang et al.) emerge as special cases with different parameter choices (α=1, 3/2)

Solves a real modeling problem: Uniquely predicts tuning curve flattening observed empirically (Padamsey et al. 2022), while competing models predict shortening or widening with firing rate homeostasis violations
Rigorous mathematical analysis: Well-derived analytical solutions for multiple coding objectives with comprehensive appendices supporting reproducibility
Comprehensive treatment: Addresses multiple objectives, activity levels, and provides thorough supplementary materials demonstrating technical depth
weaknesses: Limited empirical validation: Framework tested against only one recent dataset (Padamsey et al. 2022); lacks validation across organisms, brain regions, stimulus modalities, or different timescales of metabolic adaptation

Parameter fitting concerns: Energy budget parameters (a₁, a₂) and noise model η_κ are explicitly fit to match the empirical data being explained; high-order polynomial fitting (degree 8) raises generalizability questions; no cross-validation or sensitivity analysis provided
Approximate homeostasis constraint: Equation (5) is an approximation with validity conditions under-explored; appendices reveal violations of 0.14-0.20% suggesting potential issues in some regimes
Restrictive modeling scope: Limited to Gaussian tuning curves and scalar stimuli; single-compartment neuron model; only validated on mouse visual cortex L2/3; applicability to other systems unclear

Limited novelty: Combines existing population coding optimization approaches with a more realistic energy constraint rather than introducing fundamentally new concepts; incremental contribution despite solid execution

Generalizability unclear: Activity level parameter κ and its relationship to actual neural statistics under-justified; unclear whether framework applies beyond the specific Padamsey dataset on which it was calibrated

strengths: Novel problem formulation addressing an important, underexplored question about neural coding under metabolic constraints
Elegant mathematical framework that unifies competing models (Ganguli & Simoncelli and Wang et al.) as special cases through principled parameter choices
Thorough biophysical grounding via NEURON simulations, making realistic connections between ATP consumption, noise, and energy budgets
Clear analytical solutions for optimal population codes under varying energy budgets and multiple coding objectives
Specific, quantitative predictions (32% widening with 29% ATP reduction) that replicate empirical observations inaccessible to prior models
Comprehensive robustness analysis addressing noise correlations, non-Gaussian tuning curves, different priors, and sparse treatment in appendices
weaknesses: Empirical validation limited to single dataset (Padamsey et al. 2022) that averages across different cells; no repeated-measures validation or cross-system testing
Core assumption that neurons follow optimal adaptation paths is plausible but empirically unvalidated; no direct evidence presented
Strong modeling assumptions (tiling, conditional independence, Gaussian base shapes, uniform stimulus priors) that are only partially validated; homeostasis approximation errors ~0.2-0.5%
Narrow scope: only validated on mouse visual cortex L2/3; single stimulus dimension; no network-level effects or cross-species generalization
Model requires fitting multiple κ-dependent parameters (a₁, a₂, b₁, b₂, η₀) from simulation, limiting generalizability to new systems or cell types
Circular reasoning in energy constraint definition: constraint designed so that fitted density scales as E^(1/α), then α=1 derived from this scaling
Limited prospective validation: model explains existing data but hasn't generated testable predictions subsequently confirmed experimentally
Increased complexity through fitted parameters compared to prior models without demonstrative advantages beyond explaining one dataset

strengths: Well-motivated biological problem addressing gap between theory and recent experiments (Padamsey et al. 2022)
Comprehensive analytical framework with rigorous derivations for multiple coding objectives
Elegant demonstration that prior models (Ganguli & Simoncelli 2010; Wang et al. 2016a) are special cases of the proposed framework
Biophysically-grounded connection between ATP consumption, noise, and energy budgets via NEURON simulations
Concrete, testable predictions about biophysical changes (resting potential, leak conductance) under metabolic stress
Robustness analysis showing predictions persist with realistic noise correlations (Section N)
Mathematical rigor with detailed derivations and proofs
weaknesses: Single dataset validation: Model validated only against Padamsey et al. 2022 with parameter fitting to match known widening/energy reduction—essentially fitting to the data rather than true prediction
Problematic empirical validation: Padamsey et al. used averaged responses from different cells (29 control, 32 food-restricted), not repeated trials from single cells, limiting likelihood comparisons
Narrow biophysical scope: Only single-compartment simulations, visual cortex neurons, and one stimulus dimension (orientation); generalization to other areas/cell types unclear
Approximation quality concerns: Tiling and homeostasis approximations validated only on Gaussian/Gabor curves with specific priors; systematic analysis of failure modes absent
Dispersed Poisson noise model (Eq. 14) fit at low firing rates (μF=0.1); generalizability to higher rates and different neuron types unvalidated
Post-hoc derivation of energy constraint: Power law form ∫p(s)g(s)^α ds=E with α=1 derived from simulation fitting, not first principles; circular justification via optimal decay paths

Limited theoretical novelty: Core contribution is recognizing homeostasis should be enforced and linking energy to ATP—straightforward extensions of existing frameworks using standard Lagrangian optimization
Missing independent validation: No testing on other datasets, preparations, or species beyond Padamsey et al.
Incomplete mechanistic understanding: Paper shows when prior models fail but doesn't explain why or what principles drive the differences
Sensitivity analysis missing: No exploration of robustness to α ≠ 1, different functional forms for energy/noise relationships, or parameter variations

strengths: Novel theoretical framework combining homeostasis and energy constraints that uniquely predicts tuning curve flattening, unifying previous models (Ganguli & Simoncelli, Wang et al.) as special cases
Rigorous mathematical treatment with closed-form analytical solutions for multiple objectives (infomax, discrimax, Lp error)
Substantial biophysical grounding through extensive NEURON simulations properly accounting for ATP costs (synaptic reversal, leak currents, spikes) with <2% fitting errors
Compelling empirical validation: model predicts observed 32% tuning curve widening with 0% firing rate change, while alternative models violate homeostasis by 24-32%
Comprehensive robustness analyses including noise correlations, non-Gaussian tuning curves, and multiple stimulus priors
Clear presentation with detailed mathematical derivations and extensive supplementary materials (26 pages of appendices)
Addresses genuine gap in optimal neural coding theory motivated by recent empirical findings
weaknesses: Empirical validation limited to single dataset (Padamsey et al. 2022) with acknowledged limitations—averages across different cells rather than repeated measurements; no new experimental data presented
Key parameter α=1 empirically fit from simulations rather than independently derived; claim that it 'follows immediately' from affine fit (Fig. 3h) needs stronger justification given scatter in data

Noise dispersion function ηκ(E) uses complex 17-parameter model (Eq. 78) with risk of overfitting; additional parameters vary with activity level κ via polynomial fits—generalizability to other neuron types unclear

Approximation validity not fully characterized: tiling assumption may fail for sparse populations; smoothness conditions for approximate homeostasis (Prop. C.1) not clearly defined; small homeostasis violations (0.14-0.45%) shown but approximation limits unclear

Biological realism concerns: central assumption that neurons follow optimal decay path (Eq. 15) lacks direct evidence; mechanism for neurons to detect/implement this optimization unclear; characterized from single spikes not continuous input trains

Limited scope of empirical validation: only 1D stimulus (orientation) tested; only Gaussian/Gabor tuning curves; two priors tested; no multi-dimensional stimuli, different modalities, or network effects

Single-compartment neuron model ignores dendritic/axonal complexity; independent noise assumption in main analysis (Appendix N shows only modest additional 4% broadening under correlations, but questions remain)
Alternative mechanisms for producing tuning curve changes not explored; likelihood comparison (Sec. M.3) underdeveloped due to data limitations
